summary: Lewis & Clark County, MT lookout site 22 mi SW of Augusta; firelookout.com dates it to the 1940s with a 20-ft pole L-4 tower, abandoned in the 1950s; a 1939 newspaper plan does not clearly match that timing; gone.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; firelookout.com says Google Earth shows a foundation consistent with only a ground cab

events.note: Augusta News item of August 3, 1939, proposing a lookout on Carabau Mountain 'this season' on the divide between the Helena and Lewis and Clark forests (quoted on Forest Lookouts)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1939 Augusta News item describes a plan for that season, while firelookout.com dates the tower to the 1940s. The story reports both dates and does not choose between them.
firelookout.com describes a 20-foot pole L-4 tower but also says the Google Earth foundation is consistent with only a ground cab. The story reports both without choosing.

sources.title: Caribou Peak - FOREST LOOKOUTS (quoting The Augusta News, August 3, 1939)

notes_for_editor: firelookout.com gives only decades (1940s build, 1950s abandonment), so no year-level built or abandoned events are recorded. The 1939 Augusta News plan may not match the 1940s date; the story reports both and says neither source reconciles them. Height 6.1 m is 20 feet converted; check before publishing. Two web searches found no other account of the tower or site; the Helena/Lewis & Clark National Forest office may hold records.
